title: DevSecOps
subtitle: Build security into every stage of the delivery pipeline
audience_line: DevOps engineers and developers who own a delivery pipeline
overview: This programme adds security to a working DevOps pipeline, stage by stage, while keeping the pipeline fast. Participants model threats, scan code and dependencies, test the running application, then secure the software supply chain: hardened and scanned images, SBOMs, signatures, attestations and SLSA provenance checked before deployment. They scan infrastructure code, enforce policies as code, manage secrets with HashiCorp Vault, and harden and watch Kubernetes at runtime. The programme closes with a final project: a pipeline with a security gate at every stage and a security report.

facts.label: Audience
facts.value: DevOps engineers and developers who own a delivery pipeline

facts.label: Prerequisites
facts.value: CI/CD, Terraform and Kubernetes delivery (course: DevOps Engineering, which builds on Docker & Kubernetes), or equivalent. Pipeline building is not taught again

facts.label: Duration
facts.value: 57 h: 48 h of chapters + 9 h buffer

facts.label: Format
facts.value: Short lectures followed by guided labs; one application and pipeline carried through every phase

facts.label: Lab environment
facts.value: Runs locally: one laptop per participant (16 GB RAM minimum, Docker, kind, VS Code); Jenkins and SonarQube on a server provided by the trainer; a public GitHub repository and GitHub Container Registry per team; Terraform code is scanned, not applied; no cloud account or cost

facts.label: Assessment
facts.value: A lab validated at the end of each phase and a final project with a security report presented to the group; certificate of completion for participants who complete both

facts.label: Outcome
facts.value: Participants can add and tune security gates for code, dependencies, the running application, images, infrastructure code, secrets and Kubernetes runtime, and report the residual risk

phases.name: Foundations & Application Security
phases.focus: Shift-left, threat modelling, SAST, SCA and licences, DAST
phases.intro: Participants learn where security belongs in the pipeline and which gate stops what, model the threats of the course application with STRIDE, then add static analysis, dependency and licence checks, and dynamic scans of the running application. Validated lab: a pipeline that fails on a planted SQL injection, a vulnerable dependency and a ZAP finding, with the false positives triaged.

chapters.title: DevSecOps Principles
chapters.content: Shift-left, threat modelling with STRIDE, security gates and their thresholds

chapters.title: Static Analysis (SAST)
chapters.content: SonarQube security rules, Semgrep rules for injection flaws, custom rules, triaging false positives

chapters.title: Dependencies & Licences (SCA)
chapters.content: OWASP Dependency-Check, vulnerable dependency updates, licence compliance

chapters.title: Dynamic Testing (DAST)
chapters.content: ZAP baseline, full and API scans in the pipeline

phases.name: Container & Supply Chain Security
phases.focus: Image scanning and hardening, SBOM, signing, SLSA provenance, admission
phases.intro: Participants harden and scan the course images, then prove where they come from: an SBOM for every image, signatures and attestations with Cosign and Sigstore, SLSA provenance from the build, and admission policies that refuse unsigned images in the cluster. Validated lab: an unsigned image rejected by the cluster while the signed, attested build is admitted.

chapters.title: Image Scanning & Hardening
chapters.content: Trivy, minimal and distroless base images, non-root images, fixing findings

chapters.title: SBOM & Signing
chapters.content: SBOM with Syft, signing with Cosign and Sigstore, keyless signing

chapters.title: Attestations & Admission
chapters.content: Attestations, SLSA provenance, admission of signed images with the Sigstore policy-controller

phases.name: Infrastructure & Secrets
phases.focus: IaC scanning, policy as code, HashiCorp Vault, secret scanning
phases.intro: Participants scan the course Terraform and Kubernetes code with Checkov and Trivy, enforce rules in the cluster with OPA Gatekeeper or Kyverno, then remove secrets from code: HashiCorp Vault with dynamic secrets, its Jenkins and Kubernetes integrations, and secret scanning with gitleaks. Validated lab: a pipeline that blocks a public bucket in Terraform and a committed password, and an application that reads short-lived database credentials from Vault.

chapters.title: IaC Security
chapters.content: Checkov, Trivy IaC scanning (formerly tfsec), fixing misconfigurations in Terraform and Kubernetes manifests

chapters.title: Policy as Code
chapters.content: Kyverno in the lab, compared with OPA Gatekeeper and the built-in ValidatingAdmissionPolicy; writing and testing policies, audit and enforce modes, image verification with Kyverno verifyImages

chapters.title: HashiCorp Vault
chapters.content: Architecture, secrets engines, dynamic secrets, policies and authentication

chapters.title: Secrets in the Pipeline
chapters.content: Vault integration with Jenkins and Kubernetes, secret scanning with gitleaks, pinning third-party actions by commit SHA

phases.name: Kubernetes & Runtime Security
phases.focus: Pod Security Standards, RBAC hardening, NetworkPolicies, Falco
phases.intro: Participants harden the cluster that runs the course application with Pod Security Standards, least-privilege RBAC and default-deny NetworkPolicies, then detect attacks while they happen with Falco rules. Validated lab: a shell opened in a running container detected by Falco and an alert raised.

chapters.title: Kubernetes Hardening
chapters.content: Pod Security Standards, RBAC hardening, NetworkPolicies

chapters.title: Runtime Security
chapters.content: Falco rules, runtime detection and alerting

phases.name: Final Project
phases.focus: A secure end-to-end pipeline and its security report
phases.intro: Teams of two or three secure the delivery pipeline of a provided application, reusing the phase labs, then present the result and its residual risks as they would to a security officer.

chapters.title: Brief & Threat Model
chapters.content: Read the brief, model the threats, choose the gates and their thresholds

chapters.title: Build the Secure Pipeline
chapters.content: SAST, SCA, DAST, image scanning and signing, IaC scanning, secrets from Vault

chapters.title: Runtime & Report
chapters.content: Cluster policies and Falco rules; security report with findings, fixes and accepted risks

chapters.title: Demo & Review
chapters.content: Live demo of a vulnerable change stopped by the pipeline; questions and feedback

project.title: A Secure Delivery Pipeline
project.brief: A pipeline with a security gate at every stage: code, dependencies, running application, images, infrastructure code, secrets and Kubernetes runtime, with signed images admitted to the cluster and a security report that states what is fixed and what risk remains.
project.stack: GitHub Actions or Jenkins, SonarQube, Semgrep, OWASP Dependency-Check, ZAP, Trivy, Syft, Cosign, Checkov, Kyverno or OPA Gatekeeper, HashiCorp Vault, gitleaks, Falco, Kubernetes
project.deliverable: Repository with pipeline and policies, threat model, security report, live demo
